answer:
Promptfoo has a flag for this. Run the original eval again with `--filter-errors-only` and the ID of the earlier run:

```powershell
promptfoo eval --filter-errors-only <evalId>
```

To find the ID, run `promptfoo list evals`, or open the eval in the web viewer with `promptfoo view`.

The filter selects only the test cases that errored in that run, so network failures and rate-limit errors get retried while passing and failing cases are skipped. Results from the new run go into a new eval.

There is also a `--filter-failing <evalId>` flag, which targets assertion failures instead of errors. I'm less sure of the exact behavior of the newer `promptfoo retry` and `--resume` commands, so check `promptfoo eval --help` for your installed version. If your version doesn't have these flags, the errored test cases can still be re-run by filtering the test suite manually, but I don't know the exact steps for that.
